draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וּלְאַבְרָם הֵיטִיב בַּעֲבוּרָהּ means “and he treated Abram well on her account.” The following לוֹ refers back to Abram as the possessor of the livestock and servants listed.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and.” The preposition לְ marks Abram, a personal name, as the beneficiary of הֵיטִיב.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: The fronted לְאַבְרָם identifies Abram as the recipient of Pharaoh’s favor, and בַּעֲבוּרָהּ gives the reason, ‘on her account.’ The livestock and servants then listed show how Abram benefited.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third-person masculine singular, with Pharaoh as the subject.

analysis.evidence: In וּלְאַבְרָם הֵיטִיב בַּעֲבוּרָהּ, לְאַבְרָם identifies Abram as the recipient of Pharaoh’s good treatment, and בַּעֲבוּרָהּ gives the reason for it. Pharaoh treated Abram well because of Sarai.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בַּ combines with the masculine singular construct noun עֲבוּר to form the compound preposition בַּעֲבוּר. The third-person feminine singular suffix refers to Sarai.
analysis.sense: for the sake of, on account of, because of

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי לוֹ צֹאן וּבָקָר, לוֹ refers to Abram and marks him as the possessor. The list that follows names the livestock and servants he had.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces יְהִי, the third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol of הָיָה.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי לוֹ introduces what Abram owned. The list pairs צֹאן with בָקָר (cattle) and goes on to include donkeys and camels, identifying צֹאן as livestock.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular absolute, used collectively.
analysis.sense: flock, sheep and goats, as livestock

analysis.evidence: The phrase וַיְהִי לוֹ introduces Abram’s possessions. In the pair צֹאן וּבָקָר, the flocks and cattle are listed as groups of livestock.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. The noun has collective force.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists Abram’s possessions. חֲמֹרִים follows the flocks and cattle, and the separate listing of אֲתֹנֹת “female donkeys” supports the reading “male donkeys” here.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ “and” followed by a common noun of both genders in the plural absolute. Here it denotes male donkeys.
